bands.1:
You have won Poet Pip's badge. Now she is on your side.

"Tonight the set is a sleeping dragon," says Pip. "We are mice in its pocket."

"The film crew has gone home," says Indi. "We sneak in."

"Picture it," says Pip.

Indi's disguises are cardboard trees. Mo's label says, "PROP: BUSH (SMALL)."

"I feel a bit bushed," says Mo. Everyone groans.

Gus holds up a green balloon. "The Bogey Bomb! A month of my greenest bogeys. That's not gross. That's science. On a green screen, green things vanish on camera."

At the set, Gus pops the balloon. Splat! Everyone is green and drippy. On the Goldies' screen, the crew vanishes. Only gumboots are left.

"Floating boots," says a Goldie. "I need a nap."

The set is all fake. There are plastic trees and a paddling pool full of brown water.

A Goldie walks past. Everyone freezes like trees.

"The Reef Rays are losing by ninety," whispers Tully.

"Did that tree just talk?" asks the Goldie. He walks on.

Behind the green screen are tiny cages. The Similoon is in a cage the size of a shoebox.

Zed types PICTUREPERFECTME into a gold cabinet. Inside is an album: "SET PHOTOS. NEVER POST."

The photos show Maxx with a thumbs up. Behind him are the tiny cages.

"That's proof," says Pip.

You put the album in your bag. Wren and Pip open the cages.

Then the lights snap on. Goldies block the door with nets.

"Similoon!" cries Pip. "You are as fierce as a crocodile!"

The Similoon grows into a huge, feathery crocodile. SNAP! The Goldies run into the mud.

On the boat, you look at the last photo. It shows a giant glowing shape under the sea. Maxx has written, "FOUND HER! THE BIG ONE."

"That is Old Glimmer," says Pip. "Nobody has seen her for fifty years. And now Maxx has."

"No," says the bush.

Behind the green screen are rows of tiny cages: Likkabys, Plonketts and Whopskips. In a cage the size of a shoebox sits the Similoon, trying to be as small as a pea.

Every photo shows Maxx grinning beside the green screen with a thumbs up. Behind him are the tiny cages.

The Similoon swells into a huge, feathery crocodile. SNAP! The Goldies scream and run straight into the real mud.

"That is Old Glimmer, the great glowing ray," says Pip. "Nobody has seen her for fifty years."

She stares at the dark water. "And now Maxx has."

"Tonight the set is a sleeping dragon," she whispers, as the fog machines hum, "and we are the mice in its pocket."

Then the lights snap on. Three Goldies with nets block the only door.

"Similoon!" cries Pip. "You are as fierce as a crocodile!"

The Similoon swells into a huge, feathery crocodile with very fluffy teeth. SNAP! The Goldies scream and sprint straight out into the real mud, where they sink up to their knees.

Back on the boat, you turn to the last photo. It was taken at night, from the deck of a huge yacht. Deep under the sea glows an enormous shape, wider than a footy field. Maxx has circled it in gold pen: "FOUND HER! THE BIG ONE."

Pip goes very still. "That is Old Glimmer, the great glowing ray," she says. "Nobody has seen her for fifty years."

She stares out at the dark water. "And now Maxx has."

Indi's disguise of the Chapter is a forest of cardboard trees with holes cut out for faces. Each one has a label that says "PROP: TREE". Mo's label, for reasons Indi refuses to explain, says "PROP: BUSH (SMALL)".

"I'm not small, I'm compact," says Mo. "But I must admit, I'm feeling a bit bushed." Everyone groans, including several trees.

Gus holds up a wobbling green balloon. "The Bogey Bomb," he whispers. "A whole month of my greenest, stickiest bogeys. That's not gross. That's science."

"Why, exactly, do we need bogeys?" asks Tully.

"On a green screen, anything green disappears on camera," says Gus. "So we go green."

At the edge of the set, MaxxCam drones are circling slowly, filming everything. Gus pops the Bogey Bomb right above the crew. Splat! Everyone is dripping green from head to gumboot. On the Goldies' security screen, the entire crew vanishes against the green wall, leaving only a row of gumboots strolling along by themselves.

"Floating boots," mutters a Goldie, rubbing his eyes. "I definitely need a nap."

Inside, the set is completely fake. There are plastic mangroves, a paddling pool full of brown water, a painted sunset and a leaf blower labelled "WILD WIND". A clapperboard on a chair says, "MAXX BRAVES THE WILD MANGROVES. TAKE 47." The deep, dangerous swamp from the video turns out to be knee-deep.

In Tully's pocket, the footy radio crackles. "The Reef Rays are losing by ninety," she whispers, unable to stop herself.

The Goldie stops. "Did that tree just say ninety?"

"No," says the bush.

The Goldie shrugs and wanders off, muttering about the heat.

Behind the green screen are rows of tiny cages: Likkabys, Plonketts, Whopskips and a Humbret with its long neck bent double. In a cage the size of a shoebox sits the Similoon, trying to be as small as a pea.

Zed types PICTUREPERFECTME into a gold filing cabinet, and the drawer slides open. Inside is a gold album: "SET PHOTOS. NEVER, EVER POST. STAY GOLD!"

Every photo shows Maxx grinning beside the green screen, thumb up, teeth blazing. Behind him, in every single one, are the tiny cages.

"Each cage is a shoebox with a heartbeat," says Pip quietly. Then, plainly: "That's proof."

You slide the album into your bag. Wren and Pip open the cages one by one, and the Similoon unfolds her long neck with a happy honk.

Then the lights snap on. Three Goldies with nets block the only door.

"Similoon!" cries Pip. "You are as fierce as a crocodile!"

The Similoon swells into a huge, feathery crocodile with very fluffy teeth. SNAP! The Goldies scream, drop their nets and sprint straight out into the real mud, where they sink up to their knees. The Plonketts plonk a cheerful tune as the crew strolls past them.

Back on the Soggy Biscuit, you turn to the last photo in the album. It was taken at night, from the deck of an enormous yacht. Deep under the sea glows a vast shape, wider than a footy field, its edges rippling like a cape. Maxx has circled it in gold pen: "FOUND HER! THE BIG ONE. Finale set: need a MUCH bigger green screen."

Pip goes very still. "That is Old Glimmer, the great glowing ray," she says. "Nobody has seen her for fifty years."

She stares out at the dark water for a long moment.

"And now Maxx has."
